solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Location unspecified when year changes

indicators.note: when something changes it takes a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the two words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A calendar puzzle: where do you end up at the moment one year turns into the next?
explanation.definitionFit: Anywhere names no particular place, so it is a location left unspecified.

clue.text: Strange man in tedious climb here?

definitions.text: Strange man in tedious climb here?

indicators.note: something strange is out of its normal order, so the letters that follow are scrambled

parts.note: the three words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: An odd fellow slogging up a dreary ascent: where is he doing it?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the letters of the first part rearrange, and the question as a whole points to where such a tiresome ascent happens.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, wearisome climb is made up the slope of a peak, which is exactly the place the question asks about.

clue.text: Hard to understand inclusion of prison in area ultimately lacking

indicators.note: lacking its final part means the last letter of the word is dropped
an inclusion is something placed inside another, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the word area with its last letter removed
the can is slang for a prison

explanation.surface: A baffling report about where a jail sits within a district with missing facilities.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcane knowledge is secret or obscure, understood by only a few.

clue.text: Extremely irate after politician collecting silver becomes hoarder

indicators.note: to collect something is to take it in, so one piece is held inside the other
the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of irate

explanation.surface: A furious MP, having pocketed the silver, turns into a miser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the irate letters behind the politician-and-silver unit. The magpie is famed in folklore for stealing and stashing shiny objects.
explanation.definitionFit: The magpie is a bird reputed to collect glittering trinkets, and the word is used of a person who compulsively gathers things.

clue.text: Small weight university abandoned in the past

indicators.note: something abandoned is left behind, so the named letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A tiny measure of something that a college gave up long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means at some former time, which is in the past.

clue.text: Popular party, otherwise not held outside

parts.note: or introduces the alternative, as otherwise does

explanation.surface: A popular party that, failing other plans, stays under a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: An indoor event takes place inside a building rather than out in the open air.

clue.text: Temporary pact in Greek cases

indicators.note: to case something is to enclose it, so the outer words hold the solution within them

parts.note: the run of letters straddling these three words

explanation.surface: A provisional agreement written up in Greek legal cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases' reads like legal proceedings, but it is the signal that pact, in and Greek hold the solution across their boundaries.
explanation.definitionFit: An acting manager holds the post temporarily until a permanent appointment is made.

clue.text: One doing wrong upsetting songsters? Rare? Not entirely

indicators.note: not the entire word, so its last letter is cut off
upsetting something knocks it out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word rare missing its final letter

explanation.surface: Is it rare for a sinner to be the one who annoys singers?
explanation.definitionFit: A transgressor breaks a law or moral rule, so is a wrongdoer.

clue.text: Small, pale bird

explanation.surface: A small, pallid bird, perhaps a cygnet.
explanation.definitionFit: The swan is a large, long-necked water bird.

clue.text: Letters in order, bathe with pal at work

indicators.note: letters put to work are moved about, so they appear in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Neatly arranged correspondence, while a friend has a wash at the office.
explanation.definitionFit: The alphabet is the full set of letters of a language arranged in their set sequence.

clue.text: Some whole gales expected — special language there

indicators.note: only some of the words are used, a continuous stretch of their letters

parts.note: the run of letters straddling these three words

explanation.surface: A forecast of full-blown storms, couched in some technical jargon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There' points back to the clue's own words: the special language is found right there inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Legalese is the specialised, often impenetrable, jargon used by lawyers in documents.

clue.text: Take legal case against girl

definitions.meaning: first meaning: bring a lawsuit against someone

explanation.surface: Prosecuting a young woman in court.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to take court action against someone, and the same letters form a common female first name.

clue.text: Beginning of sale — writing material to fall in price?

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: ink is what one writes with

explanation.surface: As the sale opens, will stationery become cheaper?
explanation.definitionFit: Prices that sink drop to a lower level, a common figurative use of the word for going down.

clue.text: Regularly observed inbound sight maybe? Balderdash

indicators.note: observing at regular intervals means looking only at every other letter

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of inbound
sight is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: Was some inbound vision seen at regular intervals? Rubbish!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' signals that sight is just one example of the wider category.
explanation.definitionFit: Balderdash is foolish talk, a synonym for meaningless rubbish.

clue.text: Far from abundant incline

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to tilt or rest at an angle

explanation.surface: A slope that is anything but plentiful.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means sparse or meagre, while the verb means to slope or tilt to one side.

clue.text: Despatched to welcome hairstyle in coastal area

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside the other

explanation.surface: Someone is sent to greet a stylish haircut at the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafront is the part of a town that faces the sea, a coastal strip.

clue.text: With little confidence about eg worker's song

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: a worker ant is one type of ant

explanation.surface: A timid labourer singing, perhaps, a nervous work tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eg' marks worker as an example: worker ants are a caste of ant.
explanation.definitionFit: A shanty is a sailors' work song, traditionally sung while hauling ropes.

clue.text: One writing there's a universal God

parts.note: U is the film-classification letter for universal
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A writer declares there is a God for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: An author is a person who writes books or other works.

clue.text: Wannabe snake — I speak violently

parts.note: an asp is a small venomous snake
to rant is to speak loudly and angrily

explanation.surface: A would-be star, a real snake, admits to angry outbursts.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirant is someone hoping to achieve a position, as a wannabe is.

clue.text: Fraudulent scheme? Clear off — not right!

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter named after it is taken out

parts.note: scram is an order to go away

explanation.surface: Someone spots a swindle and tells the trickster to clear off because it is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a dishonest scheme to cheat people out of money.

clue.text: That lady would get rid of outbuilding

parts.note: 'd is the contracted form of would

explanation.surface: She would like to clear out the garden hut.
explanation.walkthrough: Three readings meet: she'd (she would), a verb for discarding, and a noun for a small hut; the apostrophe is ignored, as usual.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed is to cast off or discard, and a shed is a simple outbuilding for storage.

clue.text: Cheers advanced ability

parts.note: to advance money is to lend it

explanation.surface: A toast to gifted progress.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'cheers' and 'ta' are both casual ways of saying thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Talent is a natural aptitude or skill, a synonym for ability.

clue.text: Musician, old, is introduced to computer program

indicators.note: introduced to means put into, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a bot is an automated computer program

explanation.surface: An elderly musician gets to grips with some new software.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboist plays the oboe, a woodwind instrument, so is a type of musician.
